scenes.line1: Why does Node.js memory keep growing?
scenes.line2: How do you catch a leak?
scenes.say: Ever notice your Node app using more memory over time? How do you spot what's leaking?

scenes.label: Leak
scenes.sub: A memory leak means objects stick around when they shouldn't.
scenes.say: A memory leak happens when your code keeps holding on to objects it no longer needs. That makes memory usage creep up.

scenes.title: Start Inspector
scenes.say: To hunt leaks, start your app with the inspect flag. This lets you connect Chrome DevTools and look under the hood.
Open Chrome DevTools, head to the memory tab, take a heap snapshot, then compare snapshots to find which objects keep growing.

scenes.question: How do you catch memory leaks?
scenes.right: Use heap snapshots in DevTools or node inspect to spot leaks.
scenes.say: Interview trap: It's not enough to just restart your app. Show you know how to use heap snapshots and the inspector to actually find leaks.
